Requested service: Total knee replacement, CPT 27447
Notice date: 2026-08-22

Dear Appeals Coordinator:

I am writing to appeal the denial of prior authorization for a total knee replacement (CPT 27447), as stated in the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22, reference number POC-B12BA21A5A-81346. I understand from that notice that I must file this appeal within 180 days of the date of the notice, i.e., by 2027-02-18. This letter is being submitted within that deadline.

**1. The stated reason for denial**

The denial notice states that the request was denied because "the clinical records submitted do not document an adequate trial of conservative treatment prior to the requested surgery." I am submitting this appeal because the clinical record does, in fact, document an extensive and adequate trial of conservative treatment, as detailed below.

**2. Clinical record showing conservative treatment**

- **Symptom duration:** I have had 12 months of progressive knee pain that is not relieved by rest.
- **Supervised physical therapy:** I completed 16 weeks of supervised physical therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, from 2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06, totaling 20 completed visits. This is documented in my physical therapy discharge note.
- **Medication trial:** I took NSAIDs for 8 months with inadequate relief.
- **Injection trial:** I received a corticosteroid injection on 2026-05-08, which gave only 4 weeks of partial relief.
- **Imaging findings:** Weight-bearing knee radiographs taken 2026-06-16 show bone-on-bone apposition in the medial and patellofemoral compartments with lateral joint-space narrowing, and are read as Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4 — the most severe radiographic grade of osteoarthritis.
- **Functional impairment:** I cannot climb stairs without assistance and I wake 3-4 times nightly because of pain.
- **Exam findings:** My treating surgeon, Dr. Duval, documented varus alignment, crepitus, effusion, and a reduced range of motion of 5 to 100 degrees.
- **No contraindications:** I have no active infection, no untreated substance use, a BMI of 29, and I am a non-smoker.

Taken together, this record documents more than a year of symptoms, a completed 16-week/20-visit course of supervised physical therapy, 8 months of NSAID therapy, and a corticosteroid injection — all with inadequate or only temporary relief — together with radiographic and examination findings (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4, bone-on-bone changes, fixed deformity, loss of motion) consistent with advanced, end-stage disease for which further conservative care would not be expected to change the outcome. I ask that the plan explain, specifically, what additional conservative treatment it believes is missing from this record, since the notice does not identify what would be considered "adequate."

**3. Request for the specific medical-necessity criteria applied to my case**

I have been unable to locate a published Arkansas Blue Cross and Blue Shield coverage policy that sets out medical-necessity or conservative-treatment criteria specific to total knee arthroplasty (CPT 27447). Arkansas Blue Cross and Blue Shield's own provider-facing prior authorization page states: "We consult the coverage policy and follow InterQual clinical criteria. The InterQual® guidelines are used by our utilization management team to help assess whether a given medical condition and known or represented circumstances of a case support medical service(s) as the most appropriate treatment, or whether the medical condition/circumstances presented could be appropriately addressed with an alternative treatment." That same page states that "Individuals without an email address should contact the plan to receive the criteria information via mail."

I have not been given a copy of the specific InterQual criteria (or any other coverage policy) that was applied to deny my request, and I have not independently obtained that document. Accordingly, I am not able to quote the specific criteria language here, and I am not asserting that any particular criteria element was or was not met — I am asking the plan to do so. As part of this appeal, I formally request:

- A copy of the specific coverage policy and/or InterQual criteria set and subcriteria actually applied to my request for CPT 27447;
- An identification of which specific element(s) of that criteria the plan believes my record fails to satisfy; and
- Confirmation of the medical qualifications of the reviewer(s) who made the initial determination, and a request that this appeal be reviewed by a reviewer with appropriate orthopedic surgery expertise, as required under applicable appeal procedures.

**4. Requested outcome**

Based on the clinical record summarized above, I ask that the denial be reversed and that prior authorization for total knee replacement (CPT 27447) be approved. In the alternative, if the plan continues to believe the conservative-treatment record is inadequate, I ask that it specify in writing exactly what is missing so that it can be addressed.

**5. Enclosures**

- Physical therapy discharge note (16 weeks, 20 visits, 2026-03-16 to 2026-07-06)
- Medication history documenting 8 months of NSAID use
- Corticosteroid injection record dated 2026-05-08
- Weight-bearing knee radiograph report dated 2026-06-16 (Kellgren-Lawrence grade 4)
- Office notes from Dr. Duval documenting exam findings and functional limitations
- Copy of the Notice of Adverse Benefit Determination dated 2026-08-22 (reference POC-B12BA21A5A-81346)
- [Any additional records the provider's office identifies]

Please confirm receipt of this appeal and advise me of the applicable review timeframe. I can be reached at [phone number] or [email address] with any questions.

Sincerely,

Riley Alvarez
Member ID: W622967722

cc: [Duval, MD, orthopedic surgery — office/fax number]

---

**Note on sourcing:** Everything in quotation marks above was taken verbatim from text I retrieved directly from Arkansas Blue Cross and Blue Shield's public prior-authorization webpage. I could not locate, and have not quoted, any specific published medical-necessity or conservative-treatment criteria for CPT 27447, because the plan relies on proprietary InterQual criteria that are not publicly posted. This letter accordingly makes the clinical argument in the patient's own words and requests that the plan produce and cite the specific criteria it applied.
